Recognized globally as a Great Place to Work and the recipient of multiple partner excellence awards, BIG is built on collaboration, innovation, and delivering measurable business outcomes for enterprise clients. We are a team of experienced technology professionals who enjoy solving complex challenges, celebrating wins together, and helping customers modernize with confidence.
AN EXCITING OPPORTUNITY WITH BIG AND CONVENE AI
BIG is excited to be partnering with Convene AI, an AI-focused technology company developing innovative solutions that leverage artificial intelligence to solve real-world business challenges.
As part of this partnership, we are looking for talented professionals to join BIG and work directly on Convene AI projects and initiatives. You will initially be hired as an employee of Bits In Glass , while working closely with the Convene AI team and contributing to the development and growth of their AI solutions.
The role is expected to remain on BIG’s payroll for approximately 12-18 months, with the intention of transitioning to a permanent position directly with Convene AI following this period, subject to business requirements and transition arrangements.This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to an emerging AI organization at an important stage of its growth, while benefiting from the support, culture, and established consulting expertise of Bits In Glass .
ABOUT THE ROLE
You are the tip of the spear. You own the client relationship, the scope, and the definition of done. You decide what gets built, what does not, and when to tell a client no. This is not an internal product management role and it is not a program management role. You will be embedded with an enterprise client, running discovery, converting messy business problems into AI requirements a pod can build against, and holding a weekly release cadence together while stakeholders change their minds. Because our contracts are fixed-fee and outcome-based, your scope discipline is directly connected to whether the engagement is profitable. That is real commercial responsibility and we will treat you
accordingly.
WHAT YOU WILL DO

• Run discovery: map the current process, quantify where the pain and the money are, and identify where an agent creates measurable value rather than novelty.
• Convert business problems into AI requirements with acceptance criteria that can actually be tested, working with the AI Quality Engineer to make them measurable before build starts.
• Own the outcome definition on outcome-based contracts: what "working"means, how it is measured, who signs off, and what happens if the threshold is missed.
• Manage the client-provided domain expert: secure their time in writing up front, and escalate immediately when their availability slips. Weak domain SME support is the single most common cause of slipped go-lives in this model, and catching it early is your job.
• Manage scope ruthlessly. Weekly releases only work if the backlog is disciplined and someone is willing to be unpopular.
• Run the weekly cadence: demo to the client, capture feedback, re-prioritise, and keep the pod pointed at the highest value work.

• Own stakeholder alignment across business, IT, security, procurement, and legal, and get security and procurement engaged in week one rather than week nine.
• Partner with the client's change and adoption team so the system gets used, not just delivered.
• Track and report delivery health: burn, risk register, decision log, and benefits realisation against the agreed outcome.
• Surface commercial risk early. Scope creep, weak executive sponsorship, and integration surprises are margin erosion, and you are the early warning system.

title: Principal Security Engineer (AppSec)
description:
Hello. We’re Teya.

Teya was founded on a simple belief: local businesses deserve better.

They are the cafés, restaurants, salons, shops and entrepreneurs that bring character to our high streets, create jobs and keep communities moving. Yet for too long, financial services has made life harder for them - with clunky tools, poor support and complexity that gets in the way of running a business.

Teya exists to change that.

We’re building a financial platform for local businesses across Europe - one built around simple tools, thoughtful design and real human support. Our Members rely on us to help them run their business with confidence, and that responsibility shapes the way we work.

We move fast. We care about quality. We stay close to the detail. And we believe great performance and genuine hospitality should go hand in hand.

If you want to build meaningful products, solve real problems and make a genuine difference for local businesses, we’d love to hear from you

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're a regulated payments fintech operating across multiple European markets, scaling into banking-licence territory. Security Engineering is being rebuilt around a joint operating model with our product, platform, and infrastructure teams. We're hiring a Principal Security Engineer to own the application security side of that model: how software gets designed, built, reviewed, and shipped safely across a growing engineering estate, and how security shows up as an accelerator rather than a toll gate.

This is not a review-queue role, and it is not a role about counting findings. We're not looking for someone to triage scanner output, chase "critical" CVE counts, or sign off tickets. We want an engineer who changes how the company builds software: transforming our SDLC into a secure SDLC, placing controls where they deliver the most value for the least friction, and making the secure path the default path.

The thread running through everything here is influence. You will spend as much time with engineers, product managers, designers, operations, and compliance colleagues as you do with code and tooling. The person who succeeds in this role is the person who can walk into any team, explain the risk in language that team actually uses, and leave them better equipped than when they arrived.

WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

FIRST 90 DAYS

- Understand how we actually build. Map our real delivery paths, from idea to production, across the teams that matter most. Find where security currently lands too late, too heavily, or not at all.

- Baseline the application estate. Establish a clear, honest view of coverage, risk, and the gaps between them. We would rather know the truth early than have a tidy dashboard.

- Start building relationships. Embed with engineering teams, run threat modelling with them rather than for them, and use those sessions to demonstrate what good looks like in practice.

- Identify high-leverage controls. Identify what changes to the SDLC would measurably reduce risk while making delivery faster.

FIRST YEAR

- Secure SDLC transformation. Design and roll out the controls, patterns, and checkpoints that make up our SSDLC. Proportionate, evidence-based, and justified by impact, not by convention.

- Shift-left in practice, not as a slogan. Secure defaults in templates, libraries, and paved roads so that the easiest way to build something is also the safe way. Developers should hit guardrails rarely, and understand them when they do.

- Pipeline-embedded controls. Work with the platform team to extend policy-as-code and build upon existing pipeline security toolchain (SAST, SCA, secrets, or DAST for example). Checks that run in the pipeline and produce signal engineers trust, not noise they learn to ignore.

- Threat modelling as routine practice. Make design-stage security a normal part of how teams work, scaled through enablement and templates rather than through your calendar.

description:
Who We Are
Yellow Card is the largest licensed Stablecoin-based infrastructure provider operating across over 60 countries. From Stablecoin payment infrastructure to fiat settlement rails, wallet services, and custom local Stablecoin issuance, Yellow Card provides the complete infrastructure businesses need to manage Stablecoins, payments, and operations across 50 emerging markets.
Yellow Card operates with a substantial global team spanning 24 countries. This workforce is characterized by its linguistic diversity, with collective speaking of over 25 languages, underscoring the company’s extensive international reach.
Yellow Card Zimbabwe will operate as a virtual asset service provider (VASP) within the regulatory perimeter overseen by the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) at the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe and other relevant authorities. The entity is expected to process high transaction volumes and requires a locally based AML Compliance Officer to meet Zimbabwean regulatory requirements.
About the Role
We are looking for an AML Compliance Officer to serve as the local AML compliance lead and money laundering reporting officer for Yellow Card Zimbabwe. Reporting directly to the Group AMLCO & MLRO, who is based in Johannesburg, you will be the in-country subject matter expert on Zimbabwean AML law and supervisory expectations, build strong relationships with the FIU, other regulators, and banking and payment partners, and provide day-to-day compliance support in a high-volume operational environment. This role is ideal for an ambitious early-career AML professional with payments and crypto experience who thrives under pressure and wants to help build a regulated VASP from the ground up.
What You’ll Do
Zimbabwean AML Framework and Advisory

• Serve as the in-house specialist on Zimbabwean AML law, including the Money Laundering and Proceeds of Crime Act [Chapter 9:24], the Money Laundering and Proceeds of Crime (Virtual Asset Service Providers Registration) Regulations, 2026 (S.I. 99 of 2026), and related FIU directives, guidance, and sanctions and counter-terrorist financing requirements.

• Provide guidance and support to the Group MLRO on Zimbabwean AML obligations, FATF and ESAAMLG expectations, and the practical application of local requirements to a VASP business model.

• Translate local regulatory developments into clear, actionable advice for product, operations, customer-facing, and leadership teams.

Regulator and Partner Engagement

• Build and maintain meaningful, trust-based relationships with the FIU, the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe, the Securities and Exchange Commission of Zimbabwe, banking and payment partners, and other key external stakeholders.

• Act as the entity's resident compliance contact for registration, renewal, reporting, inspections, and information requests, ensuring responses are timely, accurate, and well evidenced.

• Represent the Zimbabwean entity in routine regulator and partner interactions, in close coordination with the Group MLRO and external counsel where required.

AML Program Implementation

• Support the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of the entity's AML program, including policies, procedures, the institutional AML risk assessment, and the customer risk-rating methodology.

• Ensure program controls reflect Zimbabwean requirements on customer due diligence, beneficial ownership, record keeping, ongoing monitoring, and internal reporting.

• Maintain robust documentation that meets the evidentiary standards of the FIU, other regulators, banking partners, and internal and external auditors.

High-Volume Transaction Monitoring and Investigations

• Review and dispose of large volumes of transaction monitoring alerts in a fast-paced environment, escalating unusual or suspicious activity in line with internal procedures and regulatory expectations.
